# Universal D&D 5e Character Sheet

A single, self-contained, **automated** D&D 5e (2014 rules) character sheet that runs in any
web browser with **no install, no server, no internet, and no Adobe, while also functioning as a beautiful pen-and-paper sheet**. The whole app — layout,
styling, and automation — lives in one file: `Character Sheet.html`.

## Why a single HTML file?
The most universal runtime on any device (Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone, Android, ChromeOS) is the
web browser. A self-contained `.html` with inlined CSS + JavaScript depends on nothing external,
works fully offline, and will keep working for years. It replaces MPMB's Adobe-locked automation
with the same kind of live calculation, in a runtime everyone already has.

## Use it
1. Double-click `Character Sheet.html` (opens in your default browser).
2. Fill it in. Everything recalculates live:
   - ability modifiers, proficiency bonus (from level), saving throws,
   - all 18 skills (with **proficiency** and **expertise** toggles), passive perception,
   - initiative, AC (from the armor you select), hit dice, spell save DC / attack, spell slots,
     carrying capacity / encumbrance, and effective speed.
3. **Ability scores** — the Abilities card shows only the final **score** and **modifier**. Click
   **⚙ Under the hood** (hidden when printing) for everything that feeds them:
   - **Generation method** — **Manual** (type base scores), **Standard Array** (assign 15/14/13/12/10/8,
     each used once), or **Point Buy** (27-point budget, scores 8–15, with a live points counter).
   - **Bonus columns** — separate **ASI**, **Racial**, **Magical**, and **Misc** bonuses per ability,
     plus a **Notes** field. Final score = base + ASI + racial + magical + misc.
   Creating a character auto-fills the Racial column from the chosen race.
4. It **auto-saves to that browser** as you type — reopening the file restores your character.
5. **Portrait** — click the box by the name to upload one (png/jpeg/webp/heic/etc.); it's shown at a
   fixed size beside the name. Click an uploaded image for a pop-up menu: **Replace / Download original /
   Remove**. The original file is stored so the download is full resolution. HEIC is kept and
   re-downloadable but only previews in Safari. The image is saved under its own key so a large photo
   can't break the rest of autosave (very large images may not persist locally — use Save to keep them).

## Pages
Tabs at the top switch pages on screen; **printing outputs every page on its own sheet**. Hide any
page you don't want via **Settings → Layout**.
1. **Core** — identity & portrait; abilities (final score + modifier, with a **⚙ Under the hood**
   generator); saving throws; 18 skills; senses & passive perception; hit dice; and Proficiencies &
   Languages. The combat area holds Proficiency Bonus, Inspiration, AC / Initiative / Speed / HP /
   Death Saves, a free-form **Resistances / Immunities / Defenses** box, an **Attacks** table (with a
   calculated *attacks per action* from Extra Attack), and a **Limited Features** tracker
   (Feature / Max / Recover / Used).
2. **Inventory** — currency (PP/GP/EP/SP/CP) with coin weight; a 34-row item table (auto item weights,
   drag to reorder, live total weight); Strength-based carrying capacity (×5/×10/×15/×30 with status);
   **Armor** (sets your AC, with AC-bonus item pickers) beside **Attuned Items**; and Equipment Notes.
3. **Features** — Features & Traits. Class, subclass, racial, feat, and background features all land
   here on character creation.
4. **Spells** — pick a spellcasting class and the sheet tailors itself: cantrips-known and
   spells-known/preparable counts, the visible spell levels, and the slot tracker all scale to your
   class & level (full / half / one-third / Warlock pact). Each row is a dropdown of your class's
   spells; hovering a spell shows its full text, with a **ritual** marker, material components, and
   "at higher levels" scaling. Auto Spell Save DC and attack. Supports subclass casters (Eldritch
   Knight, Arcane Trickster, Way of Shadow monk).
5. **Companions & Forms** — animal companions, familiars, summons, and **Wild Shape** forms. Add
   multiple creature blocks, each with a searchable monster stat-block picker (load the Monster Manual
   via Source books) and a template (Find Familiar, Pact of the Chain, Beast Master, Wild Shape, …).
   Each creature's portrait also makes its own paper mini.
6. **Background** — appearance (age/height/weight/eyes/skin/hair) + Personality / Ideals / Bonds /
   Flaws + Allies / Enemies.
7. **Backstory** — a full-page Character Backstory box.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a trimmed source-data subset for the character sheet from a local 5eTools copy.

Personal-use tool: it reads content from your own legal copy of a sourcebook (via a local 5eTools
data folder). The output (source-data.json) is copyrighted WotC content trimmed for personal use — do
NOT redistribute the data-bearing sheet or commit source-data.json.

Which book to extract defaults to the 2014 Player's Handbook ("PHB"); pass another 5eTools source code
to extract that book instead. The in-browser loader (Settings -> Source books) is the equivalent for
loading any book live; this is the offline/CLI baker.

Set the source folder via the FIVETOOLS_DATA env var, or it defaults to ~/My Drive/5etools/data.
Re-run this if the 5eTools data updates.  Usage:
    python3 build-data.py            # Player's Handbook (2014)
    python3 build-data.py XGE        # Xanathar's Guide to Everything
    SOURCE_BOOK=TCE python3 build-data.py
"""
import json, os, re, sys

SRC = os.environ.get("FIVETOOLS_DATA", os.path.expanduser("~/My Drive/5etools/data"))
OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "source-data.json")

_tag = re.compile(r"\{@(\w+)(?: ([^{}]*))?\}")

recon/r1-bugs.md:22:- **Scenario:** A large sheet (many loaded books baked, big features text) pushes the slot's main key over quota. `setItem` throws, the empty `catch(e){}` eats it, then the portrait save succeeds and `flashStatus("Saved")` runs — the user sees "Saved" but the character was NOT persisted. Next reload loses recent edits.
recon/r1-bugs.md:32:- **File/lines:** 1480 (`FEAT_SENSES.Observant`), 2792–2800 (`compute` passive calc).
recon/r1-bugs.md:33:- **Bug:** Alert's initiative bonus IS applied numerically (`featInitBonus()` at 2802), but Observant's +5 to passive Perception is only emitted as a Senses *text line*. The computed `Passive Perception` value (line 2800) never adds it.
recon/r1-bugs.md:34:- **Scenario:** Character with Observant shows passive Perception 10+WIS+prof, missing the +5 the feat grants.
recon/r1-bugs.md:35:- **Fix:** Add an Observant check to the passive computation (parallel to `featInitBonus`), e.g. `+ (hasFeat("Observant") ? 5 : 0)`.
recon/r1-bugs.md:41:### SUSPECTED HIGH — ASI/race-feat slot migration can duplicate or drop a racial feat on legacy loads
recon/r1-bugs.md:43:- **Concern:** On restore, every saved `asiChoices` entry without a `source` is defaulted to `source:"class"` (line 3043). `syncAsiSlots` then partitions by `source`, trims `classSlots` to `nClass = asiCount()`, and *separately* pushes `nRace` race slots. If a legacy save stored a race feat in the (untagged → "class") bucket, `syncAsiSlots` may (a) trim it off as an excess class slot, losing the feat choice, and/or (b) add a fresh empty race slot, so the player must re-pick. Needs a repro with a Variant-Human save made before `source` tagging existed.
recon/r1-bugs.md:44:- **Suggested check:** Load an old save (pre-source-tag) for a Variant Human and confirm the racial feat survives.
recon/r1-bugs.md:88:- **build-data.py / in-browser parity** — `DATA_VERSION = 13` in both (HTML 1209, py 26). The `et*` functions mirror the Python `*` functions for races/classes/feats/prof blocks; staleness check (`sourcesAreStale`, `init` ver compare at 4396–4398) correctly discards stored data built by an older extractor when a newer baked version exists. No divergence found that would corrupt numbers.
recon/r2-critic.md:46:If the strip contains editable inputs (not read-only mirrors), the user can edit the strip value AND the canonical input independently. Without a two-way sync handler, they diverge immediately. A one-way sync (canonical → strip on every `compute()`) solves read-only display but requires the strip to be visually non-editable — which defeats the "quick at-table tap" use case. Making it truly two-way requires either (a) moving focus between fields, which fights the browser's native input-focus model, or (b) making the strip inputs the canonical inputs (CSS reposition, not duplication), which is the only architecturally clean version but requires restructuring the DOM or using CSS `order` in a flexbox/grid, which only works if the strip and the Core tab's combat block share a flex container — they don't.
recon/r2-critic.md:49:The `.pagetabs` is already sticky at `top:0` (line 698) with `z-index:15`. A strip sticky below it (e.g., `top:42px`) would consume additional space on every tab, not just Core. On an iPhone SE (375x667) that's 42px tabs + ~56px strip = ~100px of pinned chrome before any content. The Core tab's combat section is already on-screen — the strip only helps on other tabs. The tradeoff is: non-Core tabs lose ~56px of usable height for a strip that saves one tab-switch per combat round. On portrait small phones, this is a meaningful cost for infrequent non-HP edits (limited feature uses are typically toggled once per encounter, not per round).
recon/r2-critic.md:58:The 5 high-churn fields for a Fighter with no spellcasting are: Current HP, Temp HP, limited feature uses, death saves. Spell slots are not present. The strip must conditionally hide the slot cluster or it shows 9 empty boxes. The `.slots` card already handles this via `applyLayout()` toggling `excluded` (line 2654 area). The strip would need to mirror that exclusion logic. If it doesn't, a non-caster sees a strip full of `0/0` or blank slot inputs — confusing.
recon/r2-critic.md:60:**Limited features count is variable.**
recon/r2-critic.md:61:`NLIMITED` rows exist, some blank. The strip would either show all N rows (noisy for characters using 2 out of 8 slots) or dynamically detect filled rows (requires reading `lfname-${i}` values and filtering). Neither is trivial. Showing only "used vs max" totals collapses the per-feature granularity the player needs.
recon/r2-critic.md:99:- **Content-dot tabs (`.ptab.muted` reuse for "this tab has data"):** The `.ptab.muted` class (line 385) currently means `opacity:.45` — it is used for tabs that are present but hidden (excluded pages). Reusing it to mean "has data" would conflict with the existing semantic. A new modifier class is needed. That requires: (a) auditing all places `muted` is applied (line 2654 area), (b) defining what "has data" means per tab (non-trivial: Spells tab is "has data" if any slot is used; Inventory if any row is non-empty; Features if the textarea is non-empty; etc.), (c) hooking into `compute()` to update dots after every change. This is not additive — it changes existing class semantics and requires per-tab data-detection logic. This is P1 minimum.

---
name: browser-render
description: Render HTML/SVG to a PNG/PDF image without flashing the screen. Canonical reference for headless-browser screenshots of local HTML files (rendering a generated page, character sheet, report, or canvas to an image to visually inspect it). Use whenever you would shell out to Chrome with --headless --screenshot, take a screenshot of an HTML file, render HTML to an image, or convert a local web page to PNG/PDF. AVOID raw `--headless=new` — it flashes the screen on macOS.
---

# Browser Render (flash-free HTML → image)

When you need to render a local HTML/SVG file to a PNG or PDF to inspect it (e.g. checking how a generated page, character sheet, or report looks), do NOT launch Chrome with `--headless=new`. On macOS that mode spins up a real GPU/window surface and produces a visible **white screen flash** on every launch. In a tight render→check→fix loop that strobes the whole display every few seconds and reads, to the user, like something is repeatedly taking a screenshot. (This was the cause of a real "my screen keeps flashing" report on 2026-06-03 — a render loop on the D&D character sheet.)

Important: the flash is purely cosmetic — headless Chrome screenshots a **file**, never the user's actual screen, so there is no privacy/capture concern. But it is alarming and unnecessary. Use a flash-free path.

## Preferred: `--headless=old`

One-flag change. The legacy headless mode renders fully offscreen (no window surface, no flash):

```bash
CHROME="/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
"$CHROME" --headless=old --disable-gpu --no-first-run \
  --user-data-dir=/tmp/render-$$ --hide-scrollbars \
  --window-size=1000,1400 --screenshot=/tmp/out.png \
  "file:///tmp/page.html"
```

Verified to still produce a PNG on Chrome 148 (2026-06-03), even though old headless was nominally removed around Chrome 132 — the flag is still honored. **Caveat:** confirmed it *renders*; the no-flash behavior was not visually self-verified (can't see the screen from a tool). If you switch a loop to `--headless=old` and the user still reports flashing, Chrome is likely aliasing `old`→`new` on their version — fall back to Playwright below.

## Robust fallback: Playwright (best for JS-heavy pages)

If `--headless=old` still flashes, or the page needs real JS execution / interaction (clicking tabs, waiting on load), use Playwright's true-headless Chromium — it does not create an on-screen window on macOS:

```bash
# one-time: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
python3 - <<'PY'
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch()                 # headless by default, no flash
    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width":1000,"height":1400})
    pg.goto("file:///tmp/page.html")
    pg.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
    # pg.click('.ptab[data-page="spells"]')  # real interaction if needed
    pg.screenshot(path="/tmp/out.png", full_page=True)
    b.close()
PY
```

## Other options (static HTML only, no JS)

- `qlmanage -t -s 1400 -o /tmp "/tmp/page.html"` — macOS Quick Look, native, no flash, but ignores most JS.
- `wkhtmltoimage page.html out.png` — old WebKit, offscreen, no flash; weak JS. (`brew install --cask wkhtmltopdf`)

## Cleanup

Each Chrome render leaves a throwaway `--user-data-dir` and PNG in `/tmp`. Use a unique dir per call (e.g. `/tmp/render-$$`) and sweep stale ones afterward:

```bash
rm -rf /tmp/render-* /tmp/cs* /tmp/cnd*   # stale headless profiles
```

## Rule of thumb

Default to `--headless=old`. Reach for Playwright when the page is JS-driven or the flash persists. Never leave a raw `--headless=new` in a loop that runs while the user is at the machine.

blocks.text:
Fixed. Here's what was going on.

## The bug
In the **Ability Score Improvements & Feats** wizard, when you picked "Feat," the feat list showed only a column of empty radio buttons with **no feat names** next to them. The names (and descriptions) were in the DOM but rendered at zero width, shoved off the right edge. It looked broken on **both desktop and mobile**, not just phones.

## Root cause
The stylesheet has a global rule:
```css
input,select,textarea{ ... width:100%; ... }
```
That `width:100%` is meant for text fields and dropdowns. There's a `input[type=checkbox]` override that resets checkboxes to a small fixed size — but **there was no equivalent `input[type=radio]` override**. So every radio button stretched to 100% of its row. In the feat list (`.pick-item` is a flexbox: radio + a `<details>` holding the name/description), the 100%-wide radio consumed the entire row and collapsed the feat-name `<details>` to 0px wide.

The only radio buttons in the whole app are the three in this wizard, which is why nothing else looked affected.

## The fix
Added `input[type=radio]` alongside the existing `input[type=checkbox]` resets in all three places they appear (base, print, and mobile touch-target rules) in `Character Sheet.html` — 3 lines changed. Radios now get the same small fixed width and `flex:none` that checkboxes already had.

## Verified with Playwright
- Desktop (1100px) and mobile (390px): all 42 PHB feats now show names, radios, and the ▸ expand caret.
- Clicking a name expands the full feat description.
- Selecting a feat's radio checks correctly.
- Tested via both the baked data and the real in-browser 5etools load path.

The change is purely the canonical tracked file. The baked `(Source Data)` copy (gitignored build artifact) got the same patch so it stays consistent until next rebuild. Nothing is committed — let me know if you want me to commit it.

Done. Committed and pushed to `main` (`09bdbe5..6f430a7`).

## What was wrong

Opening **Edit Character** dumped you into the wizard with **Race, Background, and Name blank and Skills unchecked** — so it looked like the whole build had been wiped, forcing you to re-pick everything. Worse, re-saving in that state silently dropped the background's features and proficiency lines (the wizard regenerates content on save, and with the fields blank there was nothing to regenerate).

## What I changed

1. **Preload the build on edit** — Race, Background, and Name are now filled in from the current character, and the Skills step pre-checks the proficiencies you already have.
2. **Protected racial ability picks** — the abilities step no longer re-derives the racial column for an unchanged race, so "choose one" ability bonuses (Half-Elf, etc.) survive.
3. **Custom backgrounds preserved** — added a small persisted snapshot (`charCustomBg`) so a custom background re-applies faithfully even if you don't reopen the Background step, and the custom panel repopulates from it when you do. It survives a page reload too.
4. **Title reads "Edit Character"** when editing (matched the button).

## Verification (Playwright)

- Standard background (Soldier) and Custom Background edit round-trips are **byte-identical** before/after — no data loss, no duplication.
- Changing race (Elf→Human) and level (8→10) on edit still work, no JS errors.
- Custom-background snapshot persists across a reload, and edit-save after reload stays identical.
- Both the tracked file and the baked copy boot with zero console errors.

blocks.text:
Done. Committed and pushed to `main` (`6f430a7..e705fa2`).

## What was wrong

On the **Race page** (the very first page of the Edit wizard), the *"Ability Bonus — your choice"* and *"Language of your choice"* dropdowns were blank, even though the character had picked them. This affects any race with chosen ability bonuses: **Half-Elf, Variant Human, Custom Lineage, and free-assign (Tasha) races**. The picks were still on the sheet, but the wizard showed them empty — so it looked like your ability score improvement was gone, and re-saving could even drop a racial proficiency line.

(For fixed-bonus races like Elf there's nothing to choose, so they looked fine — which is why this slipped through last time.)

## The fix

1. **Ability picks** — re-derived from the saved Racial column (the total minus the race's fixed bonuses) and filled back into the Race-step dropdowns. No new storage needed; works for existing characters too.
2. **Language / Custom-Lineage skill-or-darkvision** — persisted a tiny race-choices snapshot and restored those dropdowns on edit.
3. Removed the temporary guard I added last time — now that the picks are restored, the Ability Scores step re-derives the Racial column faithfully (and respects any changes you make).

## Verification (Playwright)

- Half-Elf edit now shows **Dex +1, Wis +1** and the chosen **language** pre-filled on the first page.
- Racial bonuses, languages, and features survive an unchanged re-save — including alongside a custom background.
- Elf and standard backgrounds remain lossless; both the tracked file and baked copy boot with zero errors.

One small note: on the first edit of a character whose race grants a *"choose N skills"* line (e.g. Half-Elf), two proficiency-box lines get reordered (same content, Languages now lists before the Skills line). It's purely cosmetic and stable after that first save — and previously that line was being lost entirely, so this is strictly better.

Same git-identity note as before — say the word if you want me to set your real email and amend these commits.

Done. Committed and pushed to `main` (`e705fa2..ad27ac6`).

## What I added

The Race step now shows a **full rundown** of the selected race, matching how Classes show their progression and Feats/Spells show their text. When you pick a race you get:

- **A grant summary** (head): Ability Score Increase, Size · Speed, Darkvision, skill/weapon/armor/tool proficiencies, languages (+ any "of your choice"), damage resistance, racial spells, and feat grants.
- **A trait list** (bordered box, like the class feature table): every racial trait — Age, Size, Darkvision, Fey Ancestry, Trance, etc. — with its full description text.

Examples from testing:
- **Tiefling** → shows Fire resistance + racial spells (Thaumaturgy, Hellish Rebuke, Darkness) and Infernal Legacy's full text.
- **Half-Elf** → the interactive "+1 to two abilities" and language pickers stay up top (actionable first), with the rundown below.

## Details

- New `renderRaceDetail()` function renders into a `#wiz-race-detail` box, reusing the existing class-detail styling.
- The Race step now refreshes on entry (not just on change), so the rundown appears immediately — this also fixed a latent issue where the old hint could go stale.
- Removed the old one-line "Ability: … Speed …" hint since the rundown's head covers it more completely (no duplication).

blocks.text:
Done. Committed and pushed to `main` (`ad27ac6..008db6f`).

## What I added

The race card was missing the **flavor/lore text** entirely — it only had the mechanical grants and traits. That lore lives in a separate `fluff-races.json` file, so it wasn't being extracted at all.

Now the card includes a collapsible **"Description & lore"** block with the full descriptive text:
- The evocative intro paragraph (e.g. Tiefling's "To be greeted with stares and whispers…")
- All the named lore sections with bold headers — appearance, personality, names, and society (e.g. *Infernal Bloodline*, *Self-Reliant and Suspicious*, *Tiefling Names*, *Mutual Mistrust*).

I made it collapsible (like the feat descriptions) so the long lore doesn't bury the mechanical traits, but it's all there.

## How it's wired

This needed changes in three places since the flavor comes from a separate data file:
1. **In-browser loader** — `fetch5etoolsBook` now also fetches `fluff-races.json`, and `etRaces()` attaches a `flavor` field (flattened lore sections) to each race and subrace.
2. **`build-data.py`** — mirrors that with `_race_fluff()` / `_race_flavor_map()` so the baked/offline data has it too.
3. **`renderRaceDetail()`** — renders the lore as the collapsible block.
4. **`DATA_VERSION` bumped 17 → 18** in both the HTML and `build-data.py` (the race data gained a field). Note: this means anyone with cached sourcebook data will be prompted to reload their sourcebook once to pick up the new lore — the app handles that gracefully.

## Verified (Playwright)

- Flavor renders correctly for Tiefling, Elf, Dwarf, and Human — via **both** the baked data and a live in-browser PHB load (identical 3547-char Tiefling lore from both paths).
- Edit-mode race-choice restoration still works alongside the new lore.
- Both the tracked sheet and the baked copy boot with zero console errors.

I regenerated `source-data.json` and the baked sheet locally (both gitignored), so only `Character Sheet.html` and `build-data.py` are in the commit.

One heads-up on completeness: the card now has ability bonuses, size, speed, darkvision, every proficiency, languages, resistances, racial spells, feat grants, all named traits with text, and the full lore. If there's a specific piece you still find missing (e.g. height/weight tables or creature type), point me at it and I'll add it.

blocks.text:
Done, Alex. Pushed to `main` (`008db6f..c107216`). Both of your asks are handled.

## Race selector → class selector parity
The race step now mirrors the class step exactly:
- A **scrollable list of race buttons** on the left (with the same active-highlight, hover, and border styling — I added a `.wiz-rce` class that shares the class buttons' rules).
- The **rundown detail panel** on the right (grants summary, traits, and the collapsible Description & lore).
- The choice pickers (ability bonus, language, feat) below.

Under the hood I kept a hidden `<select id="wiz-race">` to hold the value, so all the existing wizard/edit/create logic that reads `wiz-race` keeps working untouched — clicking a race button just sets it and fires the same change event.

## Racial feat picker
Races that grant a feat (Variant Human, Custom Lineage) now show a **"Feat — your choice"** dropdown right there in the race step:
- On **Create**, it materializes the race's feat slot and applies your pick (so the feat's bonuses + feature text land on the sheet).
- On **Edit**, it pre-fills from the live slot.
- The existing **ASI & Feats wizard still shows and edits the same slot**, so you can change the feat in either place and they stay in sync.

I left a hint pointing to the ASI & Feats wizard for reading each feat's full text, since the dropdown itself is just names (matching the other race pickers).

## Verified (Playwright)
- 19 race buttons render with correct active highlight; selecting updates the detail + choices.
- Variant Human + Alert: feat applies on Create, pre-fills on Edit, shows correctly in the ASI modal, and an unchanged re-save is byte-lossless (no duplication).
- Normal races (Elf) show no feat picker, no errors.
- Both the tracked sheet and baked copy boot clean.

One small thing I noticed but didn't change: like the class list, the race list doesn't auto-scroll to your selected race when you open Edit, so a selection far down the list can start above the fold. Want me to add auto-scroll-to-active for both the race and class lists? It's a quick follow-up if it'd bug you.

blocks.text:
Done, Alex. Pushed to `main` (`c107216..c1da632`).

Both the race and class lists now scroll to your current selection when you open Edit, so a race or class far down the list no longer starts above the fold.

How it behaves:
- **Scoped to the list only** — it nudges just the list's own scrollbox, never the page or the modal.
- **No jumpiness** — it only scrolls when the active item is actually off-screen, so clicking a button that's already visible never moves anything.
- One small wrinkle I had to handle: step 0 (race) renders *before* the modal is shown, so the list has no measurable layout yet. I re-trigger the scroll right after the modal opens. The class list (step 2) was already fine since you reach it after the modal's visible.

Verified by editing a Tiefling Wizard — both the Tiefling race button and the Wizard class button land in view, and both the tracked sheet and baked copy boot clean.

Pushed to `main` (`c1da632..8be4afc`). Here's what I found and fixed, Alex.

## What was actually happening
I traced it carefully. **Race** languages were already being remembered correctly (I confirmed across Half-Elf, Human, Elf, and even a full page reload). The real culprit was **backgrounds**: standard ones like Sage, Acolyte, Hermit, Noble, Outlander, and Guild Artisan grant "N languages of your choice" — but the wizard had **no picker** for them. It just dumped the literal text `2 standard language of your choice` into your Languages line. So those languages could never be chosen, let alone remembered.

## The fix
A **"Languages of your choice"** picker now appears in the Background step for any standard background that grants language choices (the count is read from the background's data):
- The chosen languages get applied on Create (no more placeholder text).
- They're **persisted and pre-filled on Edit**, just like the race language picker.
- I also strip any leftover "… of your choice" placeholder from the Languages line, which cleans up older characters too.
- Custom Background is untouched — it still uses its own combined tools+languages panel.

## Verified (Playwright)
- Sage's two languages (Draconic + Celestial) apply on Create → `Languages: Common, Elvish, Draconic, Celestial`, no placeholder.
- On Edit they're restored to the dropdowns, and an unchanged re-save keeps them with no duplication.
- Backgrounds without language choices (Soldier) show no picker; Custom Background still shows its own panel; both files boot clean.

One honest caveat: if you have a character created *before* the snapshot features existed, the wizard can't know which of its languages were "chosen" versus granted, so it won't pre-fill those dropdowns — but your languages are still safe on the sheet and never lost on edit. Anything built with the current version remembers everything. If a specific character is still misbehaving, tell me its race + background and I'll repro that exact combo.

---

# Tasha's Cauldron of Everything — PC-Facing Optional Rules (for a character-sheet app)

**Classification key:** (A) PERSISTENT-MECHANICAL · (B) CHOICE-AT-LEVELUP / SWAP · (C) NARRATIVE / PLAY-TIME-ONLY

A note on page numbers: the origin rules are firmly on **TCE p.8**. The "Class Feature Variants" live in TCE Chapter 1 in per-class subsections; I give the exact level each feature attaches to (which is what a sheet actually needs) rather than fabricating page numbers I can't verify precisely.

---

## 1. Customizing Your Origin (TCE p.8) — optional rule

This rule lets a player replace the *origin-tied* parts of any race/species. It has **three** distinct sub-rules:

| # | Sub-rule | Exact mechanical effect | Class |
|---|----------|------------------------|-------|
| 1.1 | **Ability Score Increases** | Ignore the race's listed ASIs. Instead: **increase one score by +2 and a different score by +1, OR increase three different scores by +1 each.** No score above 20. | (A) |
| 1.2 | **Languages** | Replace any language the race grants (you may keep Common or swap others) with a different **standard** language of your choice. Same *number* of languages. | (A) |
| 1.3 | **Proficiencies** | Replace a skill/tool/weapon proficiency granted by your race with a different one **of the same kind** (skill→skill, tool/weapon→tool/weapon). Primarily used to avoid duplicate proficiencies. | (A) |

**Important accuracy note for your toggles:** The TCE p.8 rule does **NOT** include "creature type" reassignment or "swap racial spells." Those two mechanics (choosing creature type, swapping an innate racial spell for one of the same level/list) were introduced **later**, in *Mordenkainen Presents: Monsters of the Multiverse* (2022), where the PHB races were reprinted. If your app targets TCE specifically, only 1.1–1.3 above belong to "Customizing Your Origin." (If you want MotM-era behavior, add creature-type + spell-swap as separate, non-TCE toggles.)

---

## 2. Custom Lineage (TCE p.8)

A full alternative "race" template (functions like Variant Human). Grants:

| Trait | Effect | Class |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Creature Type | Humanoid | (A) |
| Size | Small **or** Medium (your choice) | (A) |
| Speed | 30 ft. walking | (A) |
| Ability Score Increase | **+2 to one ability score of your choice** (or use Customizing Your Origin's +2/+1 spread) | (A) |
| Feat | **One feat of your choice at 1st level** (must meet prerequisites) | (A) |
| Variable Trait | **Darkvision 60 ft. OR proficiency in one skill of your choice** | (A) |
| Languages | Common **plus one** standard language of your choice | (A) |

Whole thing is **(A) PERSISTENT-MECHANICAL** — it sets several sheet fields at character creation.

---

## 3. Optional Class Features ("Class Feature Variants")

Covers the **12 core classes**. **Artificer is excluded** — it's presented as a full class in TCE Chapter 1 and has **no** Class-Feature-Variant toggles (see §4).

> The "**Versatility**" features (Bardic / Sorcerous / Eldritch / Spell Versatility, Cantrip Versatility, Cantrip Formulas, Martial Versatility) all trigger **"whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature"** — i.e., usable from **4th level onward**. They are all type **(B)**: a one-for-one swap of a known option, no extra persistent state.

### Barbarian
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Primal Knowledge** | 3rd (again at 10th) | ADDS | Gain proficiency in one additional skill from the barbarian list; can also channel Rage into certain Str/Dex/Con checks while raging. | (A) for the skill prof; (C) for the rage-channel |
| **Instinctive Pounce** | 7th | ADDS | As part of the bonus action to enter Rage, move up to half your speed. | (C) |

### Bard
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Magical Inspiration** | with Bardic Inspiration (1st–2nd) | ADDS (modifies Bardic Inspiration) | A creature can expend your Inspiration die to add it to a spell's damage or healing roll. | (C) |
| **Bardic Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level: replace one Expertise skill with another you're proficient in, OR replace one bard cantrip. | (B) |

### Cleric
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Harness Divine Power** | 2nd | ADDS | Bonus action: expend a use of Channel Divinity to regain one spell slot (level ≤ half prof bonus, rounded up). Limited uses per long rest, scaling with level. | (A) (adds a tracked resource) |
| **Cantrip Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level, replace one cleric cantrip with another. | (B) |
| **Blessed Strikes** | 8th | **REPLACES** Divine Strike **or** Potent Spellcasting | Once per turn, add 1d8 radiant damage when you hit with a cantrip or a weapon attack. | (A) |

### Druid
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Wild Companion** | 2nd | ADDS | Expend a use of Wild Shape to cast *find familiar* (no material components); familiar is a fey, lasts hours = half druid level. | (C) |
| **Cantrip Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level, replace one druid cantrip with another. | (B) |

### Fighter
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Martial Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level: replace a Fighting Style with another, OR (Battle Master) replace one maneuver you know. | (B) |
| **New Fighting Styles** (option pool) | 1st (or when granted) | ADDS options | Blind Fighting, Interception, Superior Technique, Thrown Weapon Fighting, Unarmed Fighting. | (A) when chosen |
| **New Battle Master Maneuvers** (option pool) | when learned | ADDS options | Ambush, Bait and Switch, Brace, Commanding Presence, Grappling Strike, Quick Toss, Tactical Assessment. | (A) when chosen |

### Monk
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Dedicated Weapon** | 2nd | ADDS | After a rest, designate one simple/martial weapon (no Heavy/Special) as a monk weapon. | (A) (changes which weapons use Martial Arts) |
| **Ki-Fueled Attack** | 3rd | ADDS | If you spent ≥1 ki on an action this turn, make one unarmed strike / monk-weapon attack as a bonus action. | (C) |
| **Quickened Healing** | 4th | ADDS | Action: spend 2 ki, roll a Martial Arts die, regain HP = roll + prof bonus. | (A)/(C) (tracked ki resource) |
| **Focused Aim** | 5th | ADDS | When you miss an attack, spend 1–3 ki to add +2 to the roll per ki spent. | (C) |

### Paladin
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Harness Divine Power** | 3rd | ADDS | Same as Cleric's: expend Channel Divinity to regain a spell slot. | (A) (tracked resource) |
| **Martial Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level, replace a Fighting Style with another available to paladins. | (B) |

### Ranger (most reworked — note several REPLACE base features)
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Deft Explorer** | 1st (unfolds at 1/6/10) | **REPLACES** Natural Explorer | 1st (*Canny*): Expertise in one skill + learn 2 languages. 6th (*Roving*): +5 ft speed, gain climb & swim speeds = walking speed. 10th (*Tireless*): action for 1d8+Wis temp HP (prof-bonus uses/long rest), reduce exhaustion by 1 on a short rest. | (A) |
| **Favored Foe** | 1st | **REPLACES** Favored Enemy | When you hit, mark a creature (concentration, 1 min): +1d4 damage once per turn (scales 1d6 at 6th, 1d8 at 14th); uses = prof bonus/long rest. | (A) |
| **Primal Awareness** | 3rd | **REPLACES** Primeval Awareness | Gain always-prepared spells (speak with animals, beast sense, etc.) castable once each per long rest without a slot. | (A) |
| **Spellcasting Focus** | 2nd | ADDS | May use a druidic focus as a spellcasting focus for ranger spells. | (A) |
| **Martial Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level, swap a Fighting Style. | (B) |
| **Spell Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level, replace one ranger spell known with another. | (B) |
| **Nature's Veil** | 10th | **REPLACES** Hide in Plain Sight | Bonus action: become invisible until the start of your next turn; uses = prof bonus/long rest. | (A) (tracked resource) |

### Rogue
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Steady Aim** | 3rd | ADDS | Bonus action (if you haven't moved this turn): gain advantage on your next attack this turn; speed becomes 0 until end of turn. | (C) |

### Sorcerer
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sorcerous Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level: replace one Metamagic option, OR replace one cantrip. | (B) |
| **Magical Guidance** | 5th | ADDS | When you fail an ability check, spend 1 sorcery point to reroll (must use the new roll). | (C) |
| **New Metamagic** (option pool) | 3rd+ (when Metamagic learned) | ADDS options | Seeking Spell (2 SP, reroll a missed attack) and Transmuted Spell (1 SP, change damage type). | (A) when chosen |

### Warlock
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Eldritch Versatility** | 4th+ (ASI levels) | ADDS (swap option) | At an ASI level: replace one Eldritch Invocation, OR your Pact Boon, OR a cantrip, OR (12th+) one Mystic Arcanum spell. | (B) |
| **Pact of the Talisman** (new Pact Boon option) | 3rd | ADDS option | A worn talisman lets the wearer add 1d4 to a failed ability check; uses = prof bonus/long rest. | (A) when chosen |
| **New Invocations** (option pool) | varies | ADDS options | Bond of the Talisman, Eldritch Mind, Far Scribe, Gift of the Protectors, Investment of the Chain Master, Protection of the Talisman, Rebuke of the Talisman, Undying Servitude. | (A) when chosen |

### Wizard
| Feature | Level | Add/Replace | Effect | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cantrip Formulas** | 3rd | ADDS | After a long rest, replace one wizard cantrip you know with another from the wizard list. | (B) |

---

## 4. Artificer — clarification

The Artificer in TCE is a **complete class** (TCE Chapter 1), not part of the Class Feature Variants chapter. **It has no separate "optional class feature" toggles** in TCE. Sources confirm the variants cover "every published class **except the Artificer**." So your app shouldn't expect Artificer-specific origin/feature toggles from TCE beyond the universal Customizing Your Origin / Custom Lineage rules in §1–§2.

---

## 5. Other PC-facing optional content in TCE (not "rules" but sheet-relevant options)

These are **additive content**, not toggle-able optional *rules*, but they expand a PC sheet:
- **New feats** (e.g., Artificer Initiate, Chef, Crusher/Piercer/Slasher, Eldritch Adept, Fey Touched, Shadow Touched, Telekinetic, Telepathic, Skill Expert, Fighting Initiate, Metamagic Adept, Poisoner, Gunner, etc.) — (A) when taken.
- **New subclasses** for every class — (A), but subclass selection is normal, not an "optional rule."
- **New spells** (incl. the psionic/Psi-dice spells) — selectable like any spell.
- The **"Supernatural Gifts"** sidebar (e.g., Blessings, Charms, Epic Boons appear elsewhere; TCE's supernatural gifts) — DM-granted, treat as (C)/(A) only if your DM enables.

**Excluded as DM/campaign-only (per your scope):** Sidekicks, Group Patrons, the Parley/encounter-building/puzzles material, magic-item tables, and the Wonders/Environmental DM tools.

---

## Quick toggle-design summary

- **Auto-apply (A):** Custom ASIs (1.1), language/prof swaps (1.2–1.3), all of Custom Lineage (§2), Primal Knowledge (skill), Blessed Strikes, Harness Divine Power, Deft Explorer, Favored Foe, Primal Awareness, Nature's Veil, Dedicated Weapon, Quickened Healing, Spellcasting Focus, plus any chosen new fighting style/maneuver/metamagic/invocation/pact boon.
- **Swap-only at level-up (B):** Bardic / Cantrip / Sorcerous / Eldritch / Spell / Martial Versatility and Cantrip Formulas. Sheet shows only the swapped result — no extra state needed.
- **Play-time only (C):** Instinctive Pounce, Magical Inspiration, Wild Companion, Ki-Fueled Attack, Focused Aim, Steady Aim, Magical Guidance (and the rage-channel half of Primal Knowledge).

Sources: [RPGBot — Optional Class Features](https://rpgbot.net/dnd5/dungeonmasters/optional-class-features/), [Tasha's Optional Class Features — GM Binder](https://www.gmbinder.com/share/-MMBqdmAen3dxArbklgi), [Eventyr Games — TCE Review Part I: Customization](https://eventyrgames.com/2020/11/17/review-tashas-cauldron-of-everything-part-1-customization/), [RPGBot — Custom Lineage](https://rpgbot.net/dnd5/characters/races/custom-lineage/).

blocks.text:
Done, Alex. Pushed to `main` (`8be4afc..ad33ccd`). Here's what landed.

## New: Settings → "Tasha's" tab
A toggle for **every** PC-facing TCE optional rule — 31 in total — all **on by default** and saved per character. Plus Enable all / Disable all buttons. Grouped as "Customizing Your Origin" then one section per class, each with a short mechanical description.

## What's actually wired up (not just toggles)

**Customizing Your Origin** — fully mechanical, in the creation wizard:
- **Custom ability scores**: every race now lets you assign its boosts to any scores (+2/+1, or three +1s via the Racial column) instead of fixed racial bonuses.
- **Custom languages** & **Custom proficiencies**: your race's languages/skills become pickers. Crucially, they **default to the original**, so you never lose anything unless you deliberately swap.
- All three restore correctly on Edit and round-trip losslessly.

**Optional Class Features** (~28 across the 12 classes): when the rule is on and your character has that class at the right level, the feature gets added to Features as a concise reminder. The ones with real math are wired up:
- **Trackers**: Favored Foe and Nature's Veil get prof-bonus/long-rest Limited Feature rows; Harness Divine Power gets one too.
- **Replacements**: Favored Foe→Favored Enemy, Deft Explorer→Natural Explorer, Primal Awareness→Primeval Awareness, Blessed Strikes→Divine Strike, Nature's Veil→Hide in Plain Sight — the base feature is dropped.

These apply on the next Create/Edit (full rebuild), so they reverse cleanly: turning a rule off restores the base feature. I verified Ranger gaining Favored Foe/Deft Explorer/Primal Awareness with the bases removed and a Favored Foe tracker, unchanged edits being byte-lossless, and toggling rules off restoring the bases.

## Two honest notes

1. **Scope calls I made.** Per my research, most class-feature optional rules (Bardic/Cantrip/Eldritch/Spell/Sorcerous/Martial *Versatility*, Steady Aim, Wild Companion, etc.) are level-up *swaps* or play-time effects with no persistent sheet math — so those are reminders, exactly as you chose. I left out the pure *content* additions (new fighting styles, maneuvers, metamagic, invocations, the TCE feats/subclasses/spells) since those are options you pick from loaded data, not toggleable rules. Say the word if you want any of those surfaced too.

2. **Default-on for "Custom ability scores" is a real behavior change**: with it on, creating a character now means assigning +2/+1 yourself for *every* race rather than getting automatic racial bonuses. That's the faithful Tasha rule and you asked for default-on — just flip that one toggle off if you'd rather have classic racial bonuses by default.

I regenerated the baked data file locally (gitignored), so only `Character Sheet.html` is in the commit.

blocks.text:
Here's the deal, Alex.

There are two copies of the same app:

| | `Character Sheet.html` | `Character Sheet (Source Data).html` |
|---|---|---|
| Size | 434 KB | 1.26 MB |
| Embedded data | empty (`null`) | ~825 KB of sourcebook data baked in |
| Git | **tracked** (shareable) | **gitignored** |

Both files are the *exact same application* — identical layout, styling, and logic. The only difference is the `<script id="source-data">` block: in the tracked file it's empty, and in the Source Data file it holds the trimmed D&D sourcebook content (races, classes, spells, feats, items, backgrounds, monsters…).

**What it's for:** it's the **fully self-contained, offline copy**. With the data baked in, you can double-click it and the creation wizard, race/class/spell pickers, the new Tasha's rules, etc. all work immediately — no 5etools server, no internet, no "load a sourcebook" step. The plain `Character Sheet.html` needs you to load a book at runtime (Settings → Source books) before the wizard has anything to work with.

**Why it's gitignored:** that baked-in content is copyrighted WotC material. Owning the books covers your personal use, but not redistribution — so the repo only ships the empty shell, and the data-bearing copy stays local. It's regenerated by `build-data.py` (which is also the offline equivalent of the in-app "Save data file" button).

One practical note from this whole session: that Source Data file is exactly what I've been driving in every Playwright test, precisely because it has the data embedded, so the wizard actually has races and classes to pick from without spinning up a server. Each time I edit `Character Sheet.html`, I re-bake this copy by splicing the data back in, so my tests run against your real logic plus real content.

So: same brain, one with the books on the shelf already, one expecting you to bring your own. The first is for sharing; the second is for actually playing offline.

blocks.text:
You're right, and it's worth being precise about *why* that works: your regular sheet doesn't have the data *in the file* — it has it in that browser's **localStorage**. The first time you loaded books via Settings, the app cached the parsed data under a `localStorage` key, and it reads from there on every open. So for that one browser, the plain file is now fully self-sufficient and the Source Data copy is genuinely redundant for you day to day.

The only real difference is **where the data lives**, which matters in a few edge cases:

- **Portability** — the baked file carries the data *inside it*. Copy it to another laptop, your phone, a USB stick, or email it to yourself, and it just works. The plain file on a fresh browser is empty again until you reload the books (and reloading needs a 5etools server running).
- **Durability** — clearing site data / "clear browsing history", a browser profile reset, or a private window wipes that localStorage cache. The baked file is immune; the plain file would need a reload.
- **localStorage limits** — the cached sources are big (~800KB+). It fits, but if you load a lot of books, localStorage can get tight; baking sidesteps that for the data.

So think of the Source Data file as a **portable, self-contained snapshot** — a backup/travel copy — not something you need on the machine where you've already loaded everything. 

Honestly, its main active use right now is *mine*: I bake it each time I edit so my Playwright tests run against real content without standing up a server. For you, on your loaded-up browser, you can mostly ignore it.

One heads-up tied to recent work: when I added the Tasha's race-flavor feature I bumped the data version (17→18). If your cached sources are still v18-incompatible the app will ask you to reload the book once. If you ever hit a "load a sourcebook" prompt on the regular sheet after that, that's why — one reload and the new cache is good.

Yes — *if* you use the right "save." There are two different things that could mean, and only one works:

**The app's built-in "Save data file" button** (Settings → Advanced) — **this is exactly it.** I checked the code: that button calls `bakeSourceData()`, which writes all your loaded books into the file's `<script id="source-data">` tag, then downloads a copy. It even names the download `Character Sheet (Source Data).html`. So you'd get a file genuinely identical in kind to the existing one: data baked in, fully portable and resilient, no localStorage or server dependence. That button *is* the in-app version of `build-data.py`, and it's literally how that other file is meant to be made.

**The browser's Ctrl+S / "Save Page As"** — **no, this won't work.** Baking only happens when you click "Save data file"; otherwise the live `source-data` tag is still empty (`null`) and the data only lives in the JS variable + localStorage. A browser page-save captures the DOM with that empty tag, so the saved copy would be right back to depending on localStorage — plus "Save As" tends to mangle a single-file app (spawns a resources folder, can rewrite the HTML). Skip it.

One important nuance about the "Save data file" button, straight from the code: it bakes in the **books**, but it deliberately **strips your current character** (it sets the character slot to `null` before downloading). So what you get is a clean, books-loaded *template* — not a snapshot of your filled-in character. That's by design: your character data is saved separately (the regular per-browser autosave / Save). So:

- Source material → yes, baked in and resilient. ✓
- Your actual character → not included; that's a separate save.

So your instinct is right: load the books, hit **Save data file**, and you've made your own resilient, portable copy. Just don't expect it to carry the character you're working on.

Good — that's a *third*, different thing, and it's the mirror image of "Save data file." I read the handler. Here's the full set:

| | What it bakes into the file | Naming | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **"Saved" indicator** (autosave) | nothing — writes to that browser's localStorage | (no file) | working day to day |
| **Top toolbar "Save"** | your **character** (not the books) | `<CharacterName>.html` | backing up / sharing a specific character |
| **Settings → "Save data file"** | the **books** (strips the character) | `Character Sheet (Source Data).html` | a portable, books-loaded template |

So the top **Save** does the *opposite* of what you're after for source material. It clones the page and bakes your **current character** into the file (`#embedded-data`), names it after the character, and downloads it. It does **not** call the bake-the-books routine, so the source data tag stays empty in that file. Open it on a fresh browser and your character shows up fine (all the typed-in values are in the file), but the data-driven bits — the creation wizard, spell/race pickers — would still need books loaded, because the books aren't in it.

In short:
- Want your **character** resilient and portable → top **Save**. ✓
- Want the **source material** resilient and portable → Settings **Save data file**. ✓
- Neither single button bakes *both*.

One non-obvious wrinkle if you want a file with **both your character and the books baked in**: click **"Save data file"** first (that routine writes the books into the live page, as a side effect), then immediately click the top **Save**. The character export will now pick up the baked-in books too. It works because of that side effect, not because it's a designed feature — so it's a bit of a hack, but a handy one. If that combo is something you'd actually want as a real button ("Save everything"), say the word and I'll add it cleanly.

blocks.text:
Done, Alex. Pushed to `main` (`ad33ccd..5862337`).

## What changed
The top **Save** button now bakes in **both** your character *and* every loaded sourcebook. So a saved character file is fully self-contained — open it on any device or fresh browser and the character *and* all the data-driven features (creation wizard, race/spell pickers, Tasha's rules) work, with no localStorage and no server. The status line and tooltip now tell you which books got included.

It's the merge you asked for: top Save = old Save (your character) **+** Save Data File (the books), in one click.

## A nice side benefit
While wiring it, I made it more robust than a naive merge. The old behavior only carried the books if you'd loaded one *that session* (loading a book happens to populate the inline data tag). After a page reload, with the books coming from localStorage, the inline tag is empty — so the old Save would've silently dropped them. Now it always bakes from the live data, so it's correct regardless of how the books got loaded.

## Verified (Playwright)
Loaded PHB into the canonical sheet, set a character name, clicked Save → the downloaded `Test-Hero.html` contained the full ~1.8MB of sourcebook data **and** the character. Both files boot clean.

Two things worth flagging:
- **File size**: every Save is now ~1.8MB instead of ~430KB (the books are the bulk). That's the cost of self-containment — exactly the tradeoff you wanted, but now you know why the files got bigger.
- **The separate "Save data file" button still exists** in Settings (it makes a clean, *character-free* books template). Want me to leave it, relabel it, or remove it now that Save covers the data? Your call.

blocks.text:
Done, Alex. Pushed to `main` (`5862337..39b3655`). All three pieces are in and working:

## XP tracker (in the Experience field)
Now a real 5e tracker instead of a blank box. It shows your current **level**, your progress (`14,000 / 14,000 XP to 6`), and pops a blue **Level Up** button the moment you cross a threshold — using the standard PHB XP table (level 2 = 300 … level 20 = 355,000). Type your XP and it updates live.

## Leveling-method choice during creation
The class step now asks **XP vs Milestone**. Pick Milestone and the Experience field becomes a permanent **Level Up** button — no XP, just click when your DM says so. The choice is saved with the character and survives reloads.

## The Level Up process
Clicking Level Up bumps your class by one level and **re-applies the whole build** through the existing wizard machinery (run headlessly for single-class, so no flashing). That means:
- New class/subclass **features** get added,
- **HP** for the new level is rolled/averaged per your HP mode,
- **spell slots** recompute,
- and any new **subclass / ASI** decisions show up as the usual banners on the sheet.

Multiclass characters route to the class builder so you pick *which* class to advance.

## Verified (Playwright)
- Fighter 4 → set XP to 6,500 → Level Up appears → click → **Fighter 5** with Extra Attack added and HP 28→34, no feature duplication.
- Milestone Fighter 3 → Experience shows a Level Up button (XP hidden) → click → Fighter 4 and the **ASI banner** correctly appears.
- Method persists across a page reload; both files boot clean.

A couple of honest design notes:
- **Decisions surface as banners, not auto-resolved.** Leveling into 3 (subclass), 4 (ASI), or a caster level doesn't force a popup — it raises the existing banners for you to click and resolve. That keeps Level Up one-click while still prompting for real choices. If you'd rather it *open* the relevant chooser automatically on level-up, I can wire that.
- **New spells known aren't auto-added** (slots are). Picking new spells on level-up is a player choice, so the Spells page is where you add them. Tell me if you want level-up to jump you there when your spells-known count goes up.

Done, Alex. Pushed to `main` (`39b3655..04f0774`).

## What changed
Level Up no longer silently bumps your first class. Now it opens the **full class-selection wizard** on the class-builder step, titled "Level Up," with a banner up top telling you how many levels you have to assign:

> **Leveling to 5.** Assign **1** more level — raise a class below, or add a class to multiclass.

From there you can either **raise an existing class's level** or **add a new class to multiclass** — exactly the choice you wanted. The banner updates live as you assign, flipping to **"All levels assigned ✓ — review HP and any new choices, then Save."** Multiclass prerequisites are still enforced (e.g. it won't let you dip Wizard without Int 13).

A couple of details worth knowing:
- **XP vs Milestone scaling**: Milestone = 1 level per click. XP mode assigns *up to the level your XP has earned*, so if you've banked enough XP to jump two levels, the banner says "Assign 2 levels" and you distribute both in one pass.
- **Normal Edit is unaffected** — it still opens as "Edit Character" with no level banner.

## Verified (Playwright)
- Level Up opens the builder with the assign banner and "Level Up" title.
- Advancing the same class (Fighter 4→5) and multiclassing (Fighter 4 + **Barbarian 1**) both update the banner and save correctly.
- A normal Edit shows no banner; both files boot clean.

One honest note: the banner is informational, not a hard gate — it tells you "assign N more" but doesn't *prevent* you from saving with fewer or more than the target assigned (consistent with how the sheet trusts you elsewhere rather than enforcing rules). If you'd rather it block Save until exactly N are assigned, that's a quick addition — say the word.

blocks.text:
Fixed and pushed to `main` (`d7f32cd..e0d3a37`).

Two things were suppressing it:

1. **The reduced-motion guard.** I'd added `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` that set the gleam to `display:none`. If you have "Reduce motion" turned on in macOS (System Settings → Accessibility → Display), that killed it entirely. Since you explicitly want this little shine, I dropped that guard — the gleam now shows regardless.

2. **The timing.** Even without that, my keyframes parked the highlight off-screen for ~90% of the cycle with a very brief, easy-to-miss pass. I retimed it to a 3.6s loop with a clear ~1-second sweep, so the white highlight visibly travels across the gold button every few seconds.

I verified it with Playwright by sampling the gleam's actual position over time — it now sweeps from off the left edge, through the button (into positive territory), and off the right — and it renders even with reduced-motion forced on. Grabbed a live mid-sweep frame too: the shine clearly crosses the "Level Up" text. Both files boot clean.

One honest note: by removing the reduced-motion guard, this animation will now play for anyone who has "Reduce motion" enabled. That's the right call for your sheet since you asked for it, but if you ever share the file widely and want to be courteous to motion-sensitive folks, I can bring back a *gentler* reduced-motion variant (e.g., a single slow fade instead of the sweep) rather than disabling it. Just say the word.

Both done, Alex. Pushed to `main` (`e0d3a37..11864ce`).

## 1. Race feat picker = the ASI feat UI
The race's feat selection (Variant Human / Custom Lineage) was a plain dropdown; it's now the **exact same browsable list** as the "Ability Score Improvements & Feats" wizard — a radio per feat with a ▸ collapsible full description, and the half-feat ability sub-picker when it applies. Picking a feat opens its description (and closes the others), just like the ASI list. Selections apply on Create and restore on Edit — verified end-to-end with **Resilient** (half-feat): its "+1 & save in" ability picker appears, the choice applies and comes back correctly when you re-open Edit.

## 2. No empty spell rows on class selection
Selecting a spellcasting class was dumping **10 blank rows per spell level** (~90 empty rows). Now, when a class is selected the spell levels start **empty** and you grow them with the existing **"+ add blank row"** button as you learn spells. A Bard 3 now shows zero blank spell-level rows.

Two deliberate choices there, so you know what to expect:
- **Cantrip rows still appear**, sized to your known cantrip count (e.g. a Bard 3 gets its 2 cantrip slots), since that's a real, meaningful count rather than arbitrary filler. If you'd rather those start empty too, that's a one-line tweak — say the word.
- The trim only fires **when a class is actually (re)selected**, not on every render, so it never erases rows you just added with "+ add blank row" (verified that still works).

Both the tracked sheet and baked copy boot clean.
